evidence.quote: We require each IFRS firm to have data in the year the firm adopts IFRS and the year before.
evidence.description: Source sample formation: non-U.S. IFRS adopters are paired with U.S. firms in the same Worldscope industry using adoption-year equity market value; pair differences above 50% are removed, and each firm-year is kept only when both pair members have data. Footnote 9 lists the aggregate Worldscope industry code groups.

evidence.quote: We estimate each full and attendant nested model using those observations relevant to each comparison we make.
evidence.description: Source defines value-relevance metrics as adjusted R-squared of the full model less an actually estimated fixed-effects-only nested model, and describes combined IFRS/matched-U.S. samples for pre/post comparisons. It also defines P at six months after fiscal year-end and country/industry indicators. The later table reports separate system rows, leaving the exact fitted universe ambiguous.

evidence.quote: beginning nine months before fiscal year end and ending three months after fiscal year end, adjusted for dividends and stock splits.
evidence.description: Source return interval is relative to actual fiscal-year end. LOSS is based on NI/P_(t-1)<0; the full fitted equation includes current-year LOSS interactions. The same page defines CF_(t+1) and its lagged-assets scaling.

evidence.quote: Pre-adoption sample years potentially range from 1992 through 2005. Post-adoption sample years potentially range from 1996 through 2009.
evidence.description: Source uses IFRS adoption cohorts 1995–2006, Worldscope Accounting Standards Applied categories “international standards” and “IASC”/“IFRS,” excludes IFRS firms cross-listed in the U.S., and reports 3,400 IFRS firms / 17,714 firm-years. All metric inputs are winsorized at 5/95, separately for years before and after 2006.

evidence.quote: where NI is net income, TA is total assets, and CF is net cash flow from operations scaled by lagged total assets.
evidence.description: Table 5 describes the cash-flow input and reports pre/post comparison sample counts; its 1,000 random assignments are inference for R-squared differences, not an extra fitted raw-data input.

evidence.quote: we estimate the following pairs of stock price and stock return regressions, pooling observations across firms and over time
evidence.description: Appendix A fits separate U.S. and IFRS accounting-system mappings by pooling observations over firms and time; the fitted mappings are then applied within and across the two samples to construct differences.

evidence.quote: including industry fixed effects and Eqs. (A1b), (A2b), and (A3b) including country and industry fixed effects.
